chunks: Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from Ibn Hashim and Ibn Yazid together, from Ibn Fadhal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The Fitra of Allah which He created the people upon,' he said: 'He created them upon Tawhid.'
ai.seo_question: What is the innate nature (Fitra) of humans according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), transmitted through the chain of Zarara, the concept of 'Fitra' is explicitly defined as the innate disposition towards Tawhid, establishing monotheism as the primordial state of humanity. This aligns with the Shia theological view that belief in God is not merely acquired but is an inherent part of the human soul's creation, often discussed in the context of the Covenant of Alast. The hadith underscores that deviation from Tawhid is a departure from one's natural state rather than a lack of innate knowledge.

en.ammaar-muslim: 3. [3/381] al-Tawhid: Ibn al-Walid from al-Saffar from Ibn Hashim and Ibn Yazid from Ibn Fadhal from Ibn Bukayr from Zurara from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام
about the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: “The Fitra of Allah which He created the people upon” [30:30]. He said: He created them upon Tawhid.
